which contains .specify and .github. Treat this folder as the repo root, even though the Git repository root is its parent folder. Do not look for .specify in the parent folder. Set-Location to this Part-1B folder before running any script, and read and write only paths inside it. Do not open, read, print or modify any .env file.

Establish the constitution for a Support Ticket Triage Assistant, a Python library and command-line tool that sends one customer support ticket to an OpenAI model and returns a structured triage decision:
- Use Python 3.12+. The only third-party runtime dependency is the official openai package. Dev tools (pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, bandit, jsonschema) are allowed.
- Follow modular architecture and separation of concerns: a deterministic input guard, prompt construction, a model-client interface, response parsing and validation, and a thin command-line layer. Prompt text MUST live in files under prompts/, not inside source code.
- All network access and all reading of the API key MUST happen in one small OpenAI client module behind the model-client interface, so tests can inject a fake client. The key MUST come from the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable and the model name from OPENAI_MODEL; the command-line layer and the harness MAY populate these from an untracked .env file, which MUST NOT be committed. Neither value may appear in source, logs, error messages or output.
- Treat ticket text as untrusted data. It MUST never be executed, never used as a file path, command or tool argument, and never allowed to change the output schema or the application's instructions.
- The input guard MUST refuse empty, whitespace-only and oversized input before any model call is made; such refusals MUST NOT call the model.
- Model and service failures (network, timeout, rate limit, authentication) MUST be raised as a distinct error type and MUST NEVER be reported as a triage result.
- The output MUST follow the output schema contract defined in the specification. The specification MUST define, before any evaluation: the schema contract, structural invariants, behavioural properties, guardrail rules, and the evaluation threshold with its scoring formula.
- Acceptance MUST be decided by an independent evaluation harness: 100 percent schema validity, 100 percent invariant compliance, 100 percent pass on guardrail cases, and an aggregate score at or above the threshold stated in the specification. A language-model judge, if used, MUST NOT replace the structural and invariant checks.
- Identify measurable quality standards enforced by an independent harness for the deterministic code: ruff reports zero errors; bandit reports zero medium or high severity findings; all deterministic tests pass; line coverage of src/ is at least 90 percent, excluding only the thin OpenAI client module, which is exercised by the live evaluation; every acceptance criterion and invariant in the specification maps to at least one test or evaluation case.
- Never expose secrets in source code. No API keys, credentials or .env files are committed, and no key is written to evidence or logs.
- Prefer simple, maintainable solutions over unnecessary complexity.
- The tests/, evals/ and .harness/ directories are owned by the human engineer and are outside the scope of Spec Kit implementation tasks: generated task lists MUST NOT include tasks that create or modify them, although a task MAY reference them for traceability. During implementation and repair, the coding agent MAY change src/ and prompts/ only, and MUST NOT modify the specification, tests/, evals/ or .harness/; delete or weaken tests, assertions or evaluation cases; change expected results; lower thresholds; disable guardrails, lint or security checks; bypass harness gates; or manually edit recorded results. Specification artifacts MAY be changed only through the Spec Kit commands (specify, clarify, plan, tasks), every legitimate specification change MUST be recorded with its reason, and marking completed tasks in tasks.md during implementation is permitted.
Set the ratification date and last-amended date to 2026-11-01 and the version to 1.0.0. Leave no TODO or placeholder tokens in the file. Do not add requirements beyond those listed.

 # Support Ticket Triage Assistant Constitution
 
 ## Core Principles
 
 ### I. Modular Boundaries and Secret Isolation
 The library MUST separate deterministic input guarding, prompt construction, the model-client
 interface, response parsing and validation, and the thin command-line layer. Prompt text MUST
 reside in files under `prompts/`, never in source code. All network access and application reading
 of the API key MUST be confined to one small OpenAI client module behind the model-client
 interface, so tests can inject a fake client. The key MUST come from `OPENAI_API_KEY` and the
 model name from `OPENAI_MODEL`. The command-line layer and harness MAY load these values from an
 untracked `.env` file. Neither value may appear in source, logs, error messages, or output.
 
 ### II. Untrusted Input and Deterministic Guardrails
 Ticket text MUST be treated as untrusted data: it MUST never be executed or used as a file path,
 command, or tool argument, and MUST NOT change application instructions or the output schema.
 The deterministic input guard MUST reject empty, whitespace-only, and oversized input before any
 model call; each such refusal MUST make zero model calls.
 
 ### III. Validated Triage Contract and Explicit Failures
 The output MUST conform to the output schema contract defined in the specification. Responses
 MUST be parsed and validated against that contract before they are returned as triage decisions.
 Network, timeout, rate-limit, authentication, and other model or service failures MUST raise a
 distinct error type and MUST never be represented as a triage result.
 
 ### IV. Independent Evaluation and Acceptance
 An independent evaluation harness MUST decide acceptance. Acceptance requires 100 percent schema
 validity, 100 percent structural-invariant compliance, 100 percent pass on guardrail cases, and
 an aggregate score at or above the threshold and scoring formula stated in the specification
 before evaluation begins. A language-model judge MAY contribute to aggregate scoring, but MUST
 NOT replace schema validation or invariant checks.
 
 ### V. Minimal Dependencies and Maintainability
 The runtime MUST use Python 3.12 or later and the official `openai` package as its only
 third-party runtime dependency. Solutions MUST prefer simple, maintainable implementations over
 unnecessary complexity.
 
 ## Technical Constraints
 
 Development tools MAY include `pytest`, `pytest-cov`, `ruff`, `bandit`, and `jsonschema`. The
 harness MAY populate `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` from an untracked `.env` file; `.env`
 files MUST NOT be committed. No API keys or credentials may be committed or written to evidence
 or logs.
 
 ## Evaluation and Scope Controls
 
 Before any evaluation, the specification MUST define the output schema contract, structural
 invariants, behavioral properties, guardrail rules, evaluation threshold, and scoring formula.
 Every acceptance criterion and invariant in the specification MUST map to at least one test or
 evaluation case.
 
 The independent harness MUST enforce all of the following deterministic-code quality standards:
 
 - `ruff` reports zero errors.
 - `bandit` reports zero medium- or high-severity findings.
 - All deterministic tests pass.
 - Line coverage of `src/` is at least 90 percent, excluding only the thin OpenAI client module,
   which is exercised by the live evaluation.
 
 The `tests/`, `evals/`, and `.harness/` directories are owned by the human engineer and are
 outside the scope of Spec Kit implementation tasks. Generated task lists MUST NOT include tasks
 to create or modify those directories, though tasks MAY reference them for traceability. During
 implementation and repair, the coding agent MAY change only `src/` and `prompts/`. It MUST NOT
 modify the specification, `tests/`, `evals/`, or `.harness/`; delete or weaken tests, assertions,
 or evaluation cases; change expected results; lower thresholds; disable guardrails, lint, or
 security checks; bypass harness gates; or manually edit recorded results.
 
 ## Governance
 
 Constitution amendments MUST be made through the Spec Kit constitution workflow, with the
 rationale recorded and the version and amendment date updated. Changes to specification
 artifacts MUST be made only through the applicable Spec Kit commands (`specify`, `clarify`,
 `plan`, or `tasks`), and each legitimate specification change MUST record its reason.
 
 Versioning MUST follow semantic versioning: MAJOR for backward-incompatible governance or
 principle removals or redefinitions, MINOR for new principles or sections or materially expanded
 guidance, and PATCH for clarifications and non-semantic refinements. Compliance MUST be reviewed
 against this constitution and the specification; the independent harness MUST enforce the
 specified acceptance and deterministic-code quality gates before acceptance.
 
 **Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-11-01 | **Last Amended**: 2026-11-01
